title: 📊 Task 1 — Maps, Plans & Comparison Charts

sections.heading: Maps and plans
sections.body:
Map questions show how a place has changed over time (two maps) or ask you to describe a current layout.

Key language for maps:
• Comparing time: "By 2020, the forest had been cleared to make way for..."
• Location: "To the north of...", "Adjacent to...", "Where the factory once stood..."
• Change: "was replaced by", "has been converted into", "a new X was constructed"
• Absence of change: "remains unchanged", "was retained", "still stands in the same position"

sections.heading: Bar chart / table comparisons
sections.body:
Comparison charts require you to identify:
1. The OVERALL pattern (which is highest/lowest/most changed)
2. SIMILARITIES between groups
3. DIFFERENCES between groups

Language for comparison:
Higher than: exceeds, surpasses, is greater than, outstrips
Lower than: falls short of, is considerably less than, trails behind
Similar: mirrors, closely parallels, is broadly comparable to, corresponds to

highlight: For maps: always write what CHANGED and what STAYED THE SAME. Describing only changes is a Band 6 approach.

example.wrong: In 1990 there was a forest. In 2020 there is a shopping centre and the forest is gone.
example.right: The most striking transformation between 1990 and 2020 was the complete clearance of the woodland area to the north, which was subsequently replaced by a large commercial complex. In contrast, the residential district to the south remained largely unchanged throughout the period.

title: 📈 Comparison Language — Avoiding Repetition
body:
Never use the same comparison phrase twice. Build a bank of alternatives:

Higher:
• exceeds / surpasses / is significantly greater than
• stood at nearly double / roughly three times
• outstripped all other categories

Lower:
• falls considerably short of / trails behind
• represents only a fraction of
• pales in comparison with

Similar:
• closely mirrors / broadly corresponds to
• shows a comparable pattern
• exhibits a similar trajectory

quick.label: Same verb twice in Task 1 = Lexical Resource penalty

question: A map shows a library that existed in 1980 but is gone in 2020. How should you describe this?
options: The library is not there in 2020.
The library, which stood on the north side of the square in 1980, had been demolished and replaced by a car park by 2020.
In 1980 there was a library but in 2020 there is a car park.
correct: The library, which stood on the north side of the square in 1980, had been demolished and replaced by a car park by 2020.
explanation:
✅ Best answer:
• Relative clause: "which stood on the north side" — adds location detail
• Past perfect passive: "had been demolished" — appropriate tense for change over time
• Replaced: "replaced by a car park" — complete picture

❌ Others: too simple, no location detail, or wrong tense

sentence: Sales of Product A _______ those of Product B throughout the period, never falling below twice the rival figure.
explanation:
"Consistently exceeded" is the precise academic phrasing:
• "consistently" = throughout the whole period (matches "never falling below")
• "exceeded" = was higher than (precise verb)

"Was more than" is grammatically awkward for this structure
"Gone up more than" implies growth, not sustained comparison

correct: Both countries experienced a decline in manufactured exports.
explanation:
Structure: Both + noun + verb + noun phrase
"Both countries experienced a decline in manufactured exports."

This structure ("Both X and Y...") is essential for comparison paragraphs in Task 1. It avoids starting two consecutive sentences with country names.

question: Which overview paragraph is Band 8 quality for a chart comparing energy use across four countries?
options: The chart shows energy use in four countries.
Overall, Country A used the most energy while Country D used the least.

Overall, it is apparent that Country A consumed substantially more energy than its counterparts, while Country D's consumption was notably lower, with Countries B and C exhibiting broadly comparable patterns throughout the period.
Looking at the chart, we can see many differences and some similarities between the four countries shown.
correct: Overall, it is apparent that Country A consumed substantially more energy than its counterparts, while Country D's consumption was notably lower, with Countries B and C exhibiting broadly comparable patterns throughout the period.
explanation:
✅ Band 8 overview:
• "it is apparent that" = impersonal academic phrase
• "substantially more than its counterparts" = precise with comparison
• "notably lower" = precise adverb-adjective
• "exhibiting broadly comparable patterns" = sophisticated noun phrase
• Covers ALL key trends in one overview paragraph

An overview should mention the MOST IMPORTANT trends — highest, lowest, and any notable patterns.
